title: Fixed and variable costs
principle: Fixed costs stay the same. Variable costs grow with sales.

screens.text: Farida's cake shop had a quiet month. Orders fell by half, but the rent bill did not.

screens.prompt: Orders fell by half. Which cost fell by half too?
screens.why: She buys one box for each cake. Rent and her helper's pay stay the same, busy or not.

screens.title: Two kinds of cost
screens.text: Fixed costs stay the same each month, like rent. Variable costs grow with every sale, like boxes and delivery petrol.

screens.title: One more cake
screens.text: One more cake means more flour, one more box and more petrol. It does not mean more rent. Rent is fixed.

screens.prompt: Farida pays her helper ₹12,000 a month, busy or not. What kind of cost is that?
screens.why: It stays ₹12,000 however many cakes she sells. So it is fixed.

wrong.a: It does not change with the number of cakes. Variable costs do.

screens.why: Rent, monthly pay and the loan stay the same. Flour, boxes and petrol grow with every order.

screens.prompt: Flour, cream and a box cost Farida ₹100 a cake. What do they cost for 50 cakes?

wrong.a: ₹100 is for one cake. She made 50.

screens.prompt: A cake sells for ₹300. Its flour, cream and box cost ₹100. What is the margin on one cake?
screens.why: Margin is price minus the cost of that one item: ₹300 − ₹100 = ₹200.

wrong.b: ₹300 is the price. Take off what the cake cost.
wrong.c: The cost comes off the price. Don't add it.

screens.prompt: True or false: if Farida sells no cakes this month, she has no costs.

options.label: True, no cakes means no costs
False, fixed costs still have to be paid

screens.why: Rent, pay and the loan are due every month, even with zero sales.

wrong.a: Only variable costs drop to zero. Rent still has to be paid.

screens.setup: Farida sells 200 cakes a month at ₹300, so she takes in ₹60,000. Each cake costs ₹100 to make. Rent and pay cost ₹22,000. She keeps ₹18,000.
screens.question: Next month she expects only 100 cakes. What should she plan for?

options.label: Costs halve too, so profit halves to ₹9,000
options.outcome: She plans on ₹9,000. She ends the month with a ₹2,000 loss.
options.why: Rent and pay did not halve. Only flour, cream and boxes did.
options.better: Split the costs: fixed ones stay, variable ones fall.

options.label: Cut her flour order in half, and stop there
options.outcome: Flour costs fall. But the month still ends in a loss she did not see coming.
options.why: She fixed the variable cost and forgot the fixed ones.
options.better: Also plan for rent and pay, which stay the same.

options.label: Rent and pay stay the same, so check for a loss
options.outcome: She sees a ₹2,000 loss coming and sets money aside for it this month.
options.why: 100 cakes bring ₹30,000. Making them costs ₹10,000. ₹22,000 of rent and pay leaves her ₹2,000 short.

summary: Fixed costs stay the same each month, like rent.
Variable costs grow with every sale, like boxes.
When sales fall, fixed costs don't.

cards.front: Your shop rent is ₹15,000 a month. Fixed or variable?
cards.back: Fixed: it is the same however much you sell.

cards.front: Paper bags for each order. Fixed or variable?
